b.x: This does not erase real danger. The body that votes to leave is still right. Watching a thought is not arguing with it all night, nor calling fear wisdom. The body now: the red page, 192. This page does not dial.

Metacognition is thinking about your own thinking. It is not a gift. It is two jobs, and both fit the gray man. The first is to notice: what thought is here, what feeling came with it, whether this is a fact or a sentence. The second is to direct: what I do with this now. Without the first, you obey the sentence thinking it is you. Without the second, you keep looking at the sentence and miss the door. The two together are the craft. See, and still choose.

The mind produces sentences all the time. Much of it is old: someone's voice, the repeated fear, the forecast of the worst, the rehearsal of a fight that is not in the room. That is not you. It is a mental event, like a noise in the street. You hear the noise. You are not the noise. The gray man trains the same distance with the sentence. It may be useful. It may be trash. In both cases, it is not the identity. The instant you say 'I am like this', the sentence sat in the chair and started giving orders. The work is to leave it standing, a visitor, until you decide whether it comes in.

The technique is short. When the sentence tightens, do not argue the content first. Put the name in front. 'I am having the thought that I will not manage.' 'I am having the thought that they are looking.' 'I am having the thought that I need to explain.' The name takes the sentence off the throne. It is still there. It is no longer an order. Ten seconds. If the body, at the same time, asks to leave, you leave. Metacognition does not veto the body. It stops an old sentence from wearing the clothes of a fact. Fact is the door, the light, the request, the child. Sentence is the rest.

It is not your defect. The mind stores more strongly what threatens. That is why the thought of danger arrives first, louder, and more convinced than the ordinary thought. It seems true because it is urgent, not because it was checked. The gray man knows this beforehand. When the sentence is catastrophe, he asks one thing only: what, in this room, confirms it? If nothing confirms it, the sentence stays a sentence. If something confirms it, it is no longer metacognition. It is the loop: see, orient, the next step. Treating every alarm as a lie is another error. The craft is not promoting the sentence to fact without one proof in the place.
The sentence wants to become speech

In the gray man, the risk of the sentence is not only inner. It wants out. It wants the table, the hall, the child, the network. Metacognition, here, is the gate. You notice the sentence before it becomes a spoken verb. 'I am having the thought of telling the fear.' Then the choice: the family needs the next step, not the film the sentence wrote. Speaking the catastrophe out loud hands the verb to the house. Watching in silence is not swallowing until you sicken. It is not confusing the relief of speaking with the duty to speak. If the sentence asks for an audience, distrust it. A thought that needs a public is, as a rule, not information. It is hunger.

It is not an hour of meditation in the middle of the street. It is a gap. Notice the sentence. Put the name. Look at the place once. Choose the step. Go. Whoever stays in the gap becomes a spectator of their own life, and the gray man is not a spectator: he is the one who still acts. Whoever does not enter the gap becomes the sentence, and the sentence acts in his place. Both errors are in a hurry. The training is on Tuesday, with one small sentence, without an audience. Repeated, the gap appears on its own in the fright. Then you discover, in the body, what the page only says: you have thoughts. You are not the thoughts. The step is yours.
